descriptionChirho: Primary prepositional sense indicating spatial origin, source, or separation—'from, away from, out of.' This is the dominant usage (649 of 651 occurrences). Spanish 'de/desde' (from/from-since), Hindi 'से/–से' (from), Arabic 'مِنْ/مِنَ' (from), Korean '–로부터/–에서' (from), Swahili 'kutoka' (from/out-of). The overwhelming majority of uses denote physical or metaphorical origin/source, making this the core sense of the preposition across all target languages.

Causal prepositional usage meaning 'because of, on account of,' indicating the reason or cause rather than spatial origin. The multilingual evidence distinctly marks this as causal rather than spatial: Spanish 'por' (because-of, contrasting with typical 'de'), Hindi 'के–कारण' (ke-kaaran = because-of), Arabic 'بِسَبَبِ' (bi-sababi = because-of), Korean '에서' (from, but contextually causal), Swahili 'kwa–sababu–ya' (kwa-sababu-ya = because-of). The causal translation markers across languages consistently distinguish this from the spatial-origin sense.

Temporal prepositional usage meaning 'since, from [a point in time],' marking the beginning of a time period rather than spatial origin or cause. Spanish 'desde' (since/from), Hindi 'से' (from, temporal), Arabic 'مُنْذُ' (mundhu = since), Korean '로부터' (robuteo = from), Swahili 'tangu–' (tangu = since). The Arabic 'مُنْذُ' and Swahili 'tangu' are specifically temporal markers not used for spatial meaning, confirming this as a distinct temporal sense of the preposition.
